Step 3: So it is acquisition of data without direct contact.
Answer: Acquisition of information about the Earth's surface without direct contact.
Similar example: Name a remote sensing satellite. Landsat.
Tip: Remote = from far away.

questions.text: Onitsha is a major river port on the
questions.explanation:
Concept: Onitsha is a commercial city in Anambra State on the eastern bank of the River Niger, with a major river port and the Niger Bridge.
Step 1: Benue, Cross and Kaduna have other towns.
Step 2: Onitsha is on the Niger.
Answer: River Niger.
Similar example: Which port is on the Benue? Makurdi.
Tip: Onitsha = Niger.

questions.text: The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in about
questions.explanation:
Concept: The Earth takes 365¼ days (a year) to revolve around the Sun, which is why there is a leap year every four years.
Step 1: Rotation takes 24 hours.
Step 2: Revolution takes about 365.25 days.
Step 3: So the revolution is about 365¼ days.
Answer: 365¼ days.
Similar example: How long is a leap year? 366 days.
Tip: Rotation = Day; Revolution = Year.

questions.text: If it is 6:00 pm at Greenwich, the time at longitude 75°W is
questions.explanation:
Concept: Time zones: 15° of longitude = 1 hour. West of Greenwich is behind GMT.
Step 1: 75° ÷ 15 = 5 hours.
Step 2: West means earlier, so subtract: 6:00 pm − 5 hours = 1:00 pm.
Answer: 1:00 pm.
Similar example: At 12 noon GMT, 30°W is 10:00 am.
Tip: East = Add (ahead), West = Subtract (behind).

questions.text: The type of rock that may contain fossils is
questions.explanation:
Concept: Fossils are preserved remains of ancient organisms. They are usually found in sedimentary rock because sediments bury and protect remains gently.
Step 1: Igneous rocks form from molten material, which would destroy remains.
Step 2: Metamorphic rocks are altered by heat and pressure.
Step 3: Sedimentary rocks preserve fossils.
Answer: Sedimentary.
Similar example: Which rock holds coal? Sedimentary rock.
Tip: Fossils = Found in Sedimentary.

questions.text: Gneiss is formed from the metamorphism of
questions.explanation:
Concept: Gneiss is a banded metamorphic rock from granite (or similar rocks) under intense heat and pressure.
Step 1: Limestone gives marble, shale gives slate and sandstone gives quartzite.
Step 2: Granite gives gneiss.
Answer: Granite.
Similar example: What does shale change into? Slate.
Tip: Gneiss pronounced 'nice' from Granite.

questions.text: The boundary between the Earth's crust and mantle is the
questions.explanation:
Concept: The Earth's layers: crust, mantle, outer core and inner core. The Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho) separates the crust from the mantle.
Step 1: Gutenberg discontinuity separates the mantle and the core.
Step 2: Lehmann separates the outer and inner core.
Step 3: So the crust–mantle boundary is the Moho.
Answer: Mohorovičić discontinuity.
Similar example: What boundary lies between mantle and outer core? The Gutenberg discontinuity.
Tip: Moho = Mountains of crust, ending where mantle begins.

questions.text: The theory of continental drift was proposed by
questions.explanation:
Concept: Alfred Wegener, a German meteorologist, proposed continental drift in 1912, suggesting all continents were once joined as Pangaea.
Step 1: Darwin worked on evolution and Newton on gravity.
Step 2: Harry Hess later proposed sea-floor spreading.
Step 3: So continental drift was Wegener's.
Answer: Alfred Wegener.
Similar example: Name the supercontinent. Pangaea.
Tip: Wegener = Wandering continents.

questions.text: Basic lava is characterised by
questions.explanation:
Concept: Basic lava is low in silica, so it is hot and runny (low viscosity). It flows far and builds gentle shield volcanoes. Acid lava is thick and sticky.
Step 1: Low viscosity means runs easily.
Step 2: High silica and explosive eruption belong to acid lava.
Step 3: So basic lava flows easily.
Answer: Low viscosity and easy flow.
Similar example: What lava forms steep-sided cones? Acid (viscous) lava.
Tip: Basic = Basalt = runny.

questions.text: The focus of an earthquake is
options: The point on the surface above the rupture
The point within the Earth where the rupture occurs
questions.explanation:
Concept: The focus (hypocentre) is the point underground where an earthquake starts. The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it.
Step 1: The surface point is the epicentre.
Step 2: The origin within the Earth is the focus.
Answer: The point within the Earth where the rupture occurs.
Similar example: Where is the strongest shaking usually felt? Near the epicentre.
Tip: Focus = Fracture point inside the Earth.

questions.text: Which weathering process is promoted by the roots of trees?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Biological weathering: roots grow into rock cracks and widen them. Burrowing animals and lichens also break rock.
Step 1: Carbonation, oxidation and exfoliation are chemical or physical.
Step 2: Tree roots act as wedges.
Step 3: So it is biological weathering.
Answer: Biological weathering.
Similar example: What do lichens release that dissolves rock? Organic acids.
Tip: Bio = Living things doing the damage.

questions.text: Material carried by a river in chemical solution is its
questions.explanation:
Concept: A river's load can be bed load, suspended load or dissolved load. Dissolved load is material carried in chemical solution.
Step 1: Bed load is rolled or bounced along the bottom.
Step 2: Suspended load is carried within the water.
Step 3: The solution load is the dissolved load.
Answer: Dissolved load.
Similar example: Which load is rolled along the bed? Bed load.
Tip: Dissolved = invisible, like sugar in tea.

questions.text: The outer bank of a meander, where erosion is greatest, forms a
questions.explanation:
Concept: At a meander, the water flows fastest on the outside bend, so it erodes a steep river cliff (bluff). On the inside bend flow is slow and deposits a point bar (slip-off slope).
Step 1: Erosion happens on the outer bank.
Step 2: Deposition happens on the inner bank.
Step 3: So the outer bank forms the river cliff.
Answer: River cliff (bluff).
Similar example: What forms on the inside of a meander? A slip-off slope.
Tip: Outside = Erosion, Inside = Deposition.

questions.text: The lowering of the land surface by wind removal of loose particles is
questions.explanation:
Concept: Deflation is the lifting and removal of loose fine particles by wind, leaving a depression called a deflation hollow.
Step 1: Abrasion is sandblasting and attrition is particles colliding.
Step 2: Corrosion is chemical.
Step 3: Removing loose material and lowering the surface is deflation.
Answer: Deflation.
Similar example: Name a famous deflation hollow. The Qattara Depression in Egypt.
Tip: Deflation = Deflates the land surface.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cold ocean current?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Ocean currents: warm currents flow from the tropics toward the poles; cold currents flow from high latitudes toward the equator. The Canary Current is cold, off north-west Africa.
Step 1: Gulf Stream, Brazil and Kuroshio are warm.
Step 2: Canary Current is a cold current.
Step 3: So the cold current is the Canary.
Answer: Canary Current.
Similar example: Which cold current flows off South America's west coast? The Peru (Humboldt) Current.
Tip: Cold = Canary, Benguela, Peru, Labrador.

questions.text: The longest river in Africa is the
questions.explanation:
Concept: The Nile is the longest river in Africa and in the world by some measures, at about 6,650 km, flowing north into the Mediterranean.
Step 1: The Congo is the second longest African river.
Step 2: The Niger is about 4,180 km.
Step 3: The Nile is longest.
Answer: Nile.
Similar example: Which is Africa's deepest river? The Congo.
Tip: Nile = flows North into the Mediterranean, over 6,600 km.

questions.text: A cumulonimbus cloud is usually associated with
questions.explanation:
Concept: Cumulonimbus is a tall dark cloud with an anvil top, formed by strong convection. It produces heavy rain, thunder, lightning and sometimes hail.
Step 1: Fine weather has fair-weather cumulus.
Step 2: Fog is a surface cloud.
Step 3: Cumulonimbus brings thunderstorms.
Answer: Thunderstorms.
Similar example: Which cloud is high and wispy? Cirrus.
Tip: Nimbus = Rain.

questions.text: The normal lapse rate in the troposphere is about
questions.explanation:
Concept: The lapse rate is the rate at which air temperature falls with height in the troposphere: about 6.5°C per 1,000 m (or 1°C per 150 m).
Step 1: 0.65°C is too small and 65°C is impossible.
Step 2: So the normal lapse rate is 6.5°C per 1,000 m.
Answer: 6.5°C per 1,000 m.
Similar example: If the temperature at sea level is 30°C, what is it at 2,000 m? 30 − 13 = 17°C.
Tip: 6.5 per 1,000: 'six and a half per kilometre'.

questions.text: Places on high plateaus such as Jos are cooler than lowlands mainly because of
questions.explanation:
Concept: Altitude affects temperature: air gets cooler by about 6.5°C per 1,000 m. High places like the Jos Plateau (about 1,200 m) are cooler than the lowlands.
Step 1: Latitude is similar, so it is not the cause.
Step 2: Ocean currents and continentality are not major here.
Step 3: So altitude explains Jos's coolness.
Answer: Altitude.
Similar example: How much cooler is Jos than a lowland place if 1,200 m? About 7.8°C cooler.
Tip: Altitude = Higher = Colder.

questions.text: A land breeze blows
options: From sea to land at night
From land to sea by day
From sea to land by day
From land to sea at night
questions.explanation:
Concept: Sea and land breezes: by day the land is hotter, so a sea breeze blows from sea to land; at night the land cools quicker, so a land breeze blows from land to sea.
Step 1: At night land is cooler than sea.
Step 2: Air over the warm sea rises, and cooler air flows out from the land.
Step 3: So a land breeze blows from land to sea.
Answer: From land to sea at night.
Similar example: Which breeze blows by day? The sea breeze.
Tip: Land breeze = Leaves the land at night.

questions.text: A thick, fire-resistant bark is an adaptation of
questions.explanation:
Concept: Savanna trees have thick, fire-resistant bark to survive annual bush fires, plus deep roots, small leaves and umbrella crowns.
Step 1: Mangroves have stilt roots, rainforest trees have thin bark and cacti are desert plants.
Step 2: So thick bark suits savanna trees.
Answer: Savanna trees.
Similar example: Name a savanna tree. Baobab or shea butter tree.
Tip: Savanna = Surviving fires.

questions.text: Soil acidity can be reduced by adding
questions.explanation:
Concept: Liming soil (adding calcium carbonate or lime) neutralises acidity and raises pH.
Step 1: Sulphur and ammonium sulphate make soil more acidic.
Step 2: Peat is acidic.
Step 3: Lime reduces acidity.
Answer: Lime.
Similar example: What does a pH below 7 indicate? Acid soil.
Tip: Lime = Less acid.

questions.text: Which of the following is a mineral used for making iron and steel?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Iron ore (haematite, magnetite) is smelted with coke and limestone to make iron and steel.
Step 1: Bauxite is for aluminium.
Step 2: Tin ore is for tin.
Step 3: Salt is not a metal ore.
Answer: Iron ore.
Similar example: What is the main ore of tin? Cassiterite.
Tip: Iron ore → Steel.

questions.text: Which of the following is a human-induced environmental hazard?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Human-induced hazards are caused or worsened by people: oil spills, pollution, deforestation, gas flaring. Natural hazards are earthquakes, tsunamis and eruptions.
Step 1: Earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanic eruptions are natural.
Step 2: Oil spillage results from human activity such as pipeline leaks.
Answer: Oil spillage.
Similar example: Name another human-induced hazard. Gas flaring.
Tip: Human-induced = Man-made.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of sustainable resource use?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Sustainable resource use meets today's needs without destroying the resource for the future. Selective logging with replanting keeps forests renewable.
Step 1: Clear-felling, bush burning and overfishing destroy resources.
Step 2: Cutting some trees and replanting others sustains the forest.
Answer: Selective logging combined with replanting.
Similar example: Which practice is also sustainable? Crop rotation.
Tip: Sustainable = Sustains the future.

questions.text: A population pyramid that is narrow at the base suggests
questions.explanation:
Concept: A narrow base on a population pyramid means fewer young people, so the birth rate has fallen. This pattern is common in developed countries.
Step 1: A wide base shows a high birth rate.
Step 2: A narrow base shows few children being born.
Step 3: So it suggests a low birth rate.
Answer: A low birth rate.
Similar example: What shape shows a rapidly growing population? A wide base.
Tip: Base = Babies.

questions.text: People who flee their country because of war or persecution are
questions.explanation:
Concept: A refugee is someone who flees their country because of war, persecution or disaster. Immigrants move voluntarily, usually for work or better life.
Step 1: Tourists travel for leisure, nomads move with herds.
Step 2: Fleeing war = refugee.
Answer: Refugees.
Similar example: What are displaced people within their own country called? Internally displaced persons (IDPs).
Tip: Refugee = Run from danger.

questions.text: Which of the following is a root crop?
questions.explanation:
Concept: Root crops grow underground as storage organs: cassava, yam, cocoyam and sweet potato.
Step 1: Maize and groundnut are cereal and legume crops.
Step 2: Cocoa is a tree crop.
Step 3: Cassava is a root crop.
Answer: Cassava.
Similar example: Is yam a root crop? Yes, it is a tuber.
Tip: Root crop = Underground food: cassava, yam.

questions.text: A cement factory is best located near
questions.explanation:
Concept: Industrial location depends on raw materials, markets, power, transport and labour. Bulky raw materials pull the industry toward the source.
Step 1: Cement uses heavy limestone.
Step 2: Transporting limestone is costly, so the factory is built near it.
Answer: Limestone deposits.
Similar example: Where are cement plants found in Nigeria? Ewekoro (Ogun), Obajana (Kogi), Sokoto.
Tip: Bulky materials = Build the factory beside them.

questions.text: Urbanisation refers to
options: An increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities
questions.explanation:
Concept: Urbanisation is the increase in the share of a country's population living in towns and cities, due to rural–urban migration and natural increase.
Step 1: Movement to villages is counter-urbanisation.
Step 2: Growth of towns relative to rural areas is urbanisation.
Answer: An increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities.
Similar example: Name the fastest-growing Nigerian city. Lagos.
Tip: Urban = Urbanisation = people to the city.

questions.text: The Niger and Benue rivers meet at
questions.explanation:
Concept: The River Niger and River Benue meet at Lokoja in Kogi State and flow together to the Atlantic through the Niger Delta.
Step 1: Onitsha, Makurdi and Jebba are on the rivers but are not the confluence.
Step 2: Lokoja is the confluence town.
Answer: Lokoja.
Similar example: Which river forms the 'Y' with the Niger? The Benue.
Tip: Lokoja = Link of two rivers.

questions.text: Nigeria's major seaport is
questions.explanation:
Concept: Nigeria's main seaports include Apapa and Tin Can Island (Lagos), Port Harcourt, Calabar, Warri and Onne.
Step 1: Apapa in Lagos handles the largest share of cargo.
Step 2: So the major seaport is Apapa.
Answer: Apapa (Lagos).
Similar example: Which port lies on the Cross River estuary? Calabar.
Tip: Apapa = Lagos biggest port.

questions.text: The ECOWAS Standby Force is mainly meant for
options: Peacekeeping and conflict prevention in the region
questions.explanation:
Concept: ECOWAS Standby Force and ECOMOG are regional peacekeeping forces for conflict prevention, peacekeeping and humanitarian action in West Africa.
Step 1: Tax collection, oil exploration and schools are not its aims.
Step 2: So the Standby Force is for peacekeeping and conflict prevention.
Answer: Peacekeeping and conflict prevention in the region.
Similar example: Which earlier ECOWAS force intervened in Liberia? ECOMOG.
Tip: Standby = Security for the region.

questions.text: On a topographical map, rivers and lakes are usually shown in
questions.explanation:
Concept: On topographical maps colours have fixed meanings: blue for water (rivers, lakes, sea), green for vegetation, brown for contours and relief, black for man-made features.
Step 1: Rivers and lakes are water features.
Step 2: Water is conventionally shown in blue.
Step 3: Brown is for contours and green for vegetation.
Answer: Blue.
Similar example: What colour shows contours? Brown.
Tip: Blue = Water.

questions.text: The vertical distance between successive contour lines is the
questions.explanation:
Concept: The contour interval is the constant vertical difference in height between successive contour lines on a map.
Step 1: Contours are drawn at regular heights, e.g. every 20 m.
Step 2: The height difference between neighbouring lines is the contour interval.
Step 3: Gradient is steepness and spot height is a single point height.
Answer: Contour interval.
Similar example: If contours are at 100 m, 120 m, 140 m, what is the interval? 20 m.
Tip: Interval = Interval of height.

questions.text: A map has an RF of 1:200,000. A distance of 8 cm on the map represents
questions.explanation:
Concept: Ground distance = map distance × scale denominator, then convert units.
Step 1: 8 cm × 200,000 = 1,600,000 cm.
Step 2: 1,600,000 ÷ 100,000 = 16 km.
Answer: 16 km.
Similar example: 5 cm on 1:200,000 = 10 km.
Tip: 200,000 cm = 2 km, so each cm is 2 km: 8 × 2 = 16 km.

questions.text: A 10 km straight road is 5 cm long on a map. The scale of the map is
questions.explanation:
Concept: Scale denominator = ground distance ÷ map distance, in the same units.
Step 1: 10 km = 1,000,000 cm.
Step 2: Ground ÷ map = 1,000,000 ÷ 5 = 200,000.
Step 3: So the scale is 1:200,000.
Answer: 1:200,000.
Similar example: 6 km on a 3 cm line gives 600,000 ÷ 3 = 200,000, so 1:200,000.
Tip: Convert km to cm first, then divide by the map length.

questions.text: Triangulation in surveying involves
options: A network of triangles with measured angles and a base line
questions.explanation:
Concept: Triangulation is a surveying method in which a baseline is measured and angles to distant points are measured with a theodolite. A network of triangles then fixes the positions of all points by trigonometry.
Step 1: Triangulation relies on triangles.
Step 2: One side (the base line) and the angles give the other sides.
Step 3: So it uses a network of triangles with measured angles and a baseline.
Answer: A network of triangles with measured angles and a base line.
Similar example: Which instrument measures the angles? The theodolite.
Tip: Tri = three sides: triangle network.

questions.text: The mean of 5, 7, 8, 10 and 15 is
questions.explanation:
Concept: Mean = sum of values ÷ number of values.
Step 1: Sum: 5 + 7 + 8 + 10 + 15 = 45.
Step 2: Number of values = 5.
Step 3: Mean = 45 ÷ 5 = 9.
Answer: 9.
Similar example: Mean of 2, 4, 6 = 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
Tip: Add first, divide second.

questions.text: A scatter graph is used to show
questions.explanation:
Concept: A scatter graph plots pairs of values as points to show correlation between two variables, such as rainfall and crop yield.
Step 1: Pie charts show shares and line graphs show trends over time.
Step 2: Histograms show frequency.
Step 3: Points showing relationship = scatter graph.
Answer: The relationship between two variables.
Similar example: What do points rising from lower left to upper right show? Positive correlation.
Tip: Scatter = Spread of points to show a Relationship.

questions.text: Which of the following is a use of GIS?
options: Mapping and analysing spatial data for urban planning
questions.explanation:
Concept: A GIS captures, stores, analyses and presents spatial data. Uses include urban planning, disaster management, locating schools and hospitals, and tracking land use.
Step 1: Predicting lottery results, typing documents and compressing music are not GIS tasks.
Step 2: Mapping and analysing spatial data for planning is a GIS use.
Answer: Mapping and analysing spatial data for urban planning.
Similar example: Name another GIS use. Monitoring deforestation.
Tip: GIS = Geography + Information + Systems for planning.

questions.text: The Shiroro Dam is built on the River
questions.explanation:
Concept: The Shiroro Dam in Niger State is built on the Kaduna River and provides hydroelectric power.
Step 1: Niger, Benue and Sokoto are other rivers.
Step 2: Shiroro is on the Kaduna River.
Answer: Kaduna.
Similar example: Which dam is on the River Niger? Kainji.
Tip: Shiroro = Kaduna River.

topic_questions.text: The true shape of the Earth is best described as
topic_questions.explanation: The Earth is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, giving an oblate spheroid shape.

topic_questions.text: The Earth completes one rotation on its axis in approximately
topic_questions.explanation: One rotation takes about 24 hours and causes day and night.

topic_questions.text: The Earth completes one revolution round the Sun in about
topic_questions.explanation: One revolution takes about 365¼ days, which is a year.

topic_questions.text: Day and night are caused mainly by the
options: revolution of the Earth round the Sun
rotation of the Earth on its axis
topic_questions.explanation: As the Earth rotates, the part facing the Sun has day while the opposite part has night.

topic_questions.text: The changing of the seasons is mainly due to the
options: distance of the Moon from the Earth
revolution of the Earth and the tilt of its axis
topic_questions.explanation: Revolution combined with the tilted axis changes the angle at which the Sun's rays strike different places during the year.

topic_questions.text: The Earth's axis is inclined to the plane of its orbit at an angle of about
topic_questions.explanation: The axis is inclined at 66½° to the orbital plane, which means a tilt of 23½° from the vertical.

topic_questions.text: The latitude of the Equator is
topic_questions.explanation: The Equator is the line of 0° latitude dividing the Earth into northern and southern hemispheres.

topic_questions.text: The Tropic of Cancer is located at latitude
topic_questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer lies 23½° north of the Equator.

topic_questions.text: The Tropic of Capricorn is located at latitude
topic_questions.explanation: The Tropic of Capricorn lies 23½° south of the Equator.

topic_questions.text: The Arctic Circle is located at latitude
topic_questions.explanation: The Arctic Circle lies 66½° north of the Equator.

topic_questions.text: The Antarctic Circle is located at latitude
topic_questions.explanation: The Antarctic Circle lies 66½° south of the Equator.

topic_questions.text: The Prime Meridian passes through
topic_questions.explanation: The 0° longitude line passes through the Royal Observatory at Greenwich.

topic_questions.text: The Earth rotates on its axis from
topic_questions.explanation: The Earth turns eastward, which is why the Sun appears to rise in the east.

topic_questions.text: The Earth rotates through how many degrees of longitude in one hour?
topic_questions.explanation: 360° divided by 24 hours gives 15° per hour.

topic_questions.text: When it is 12 noon at Greenwich, the local time at longitude 45°E is
topic_questions.explanation: 45° ÷ 15° = 3 hours. Places east of Greenwich are ahead, so the time is 3:00 p.m.

topic_questions.text: When it is 12 noon at Greenwich, the local time at longitude 60°W is
topic_questions.explanation: 60° ÷ 15° = 4 hours. Places west of Greenwich are behind, so the time is 8:00 a.m.

topic_questions.text: Every four years an extra day is added to February because
options: the Earth takes about 365¼ days to orbit the Sun
the Sun moves round the Earth
the Moon orbits the Earth every 28 days
topic_questions.explanation: The extra quarter days add up to one full day every four years, giving a leap year.

topic_questions.text: On about 21st June, the Sun is directly overhead at the
topic_questions.explanation: The June solstice occurs when the Sun is overhead at 23½°N.

topic_questions.text: On about 22nd December, the Sun is directly overhead at the
topic_questions.explanation: The December solstice occurs when the Sun is overhead at 23½°S.

topic_questions.text: The Sun is directly overhead at the Equator on
topic_questions.explanation: These dates are the equinoxes, when day and night are about equal everywhere.

topic_questions.text: The planet nearest to the Sun is
topic_questions.explanation: Mercury is the first planet from the Sun, and Earth is the third.

topic_questions.text: From the surface to the centre, the correct order of the Earth's layers is
topic_questions.explanation: The outermost layer is the crust, followed by the mantle and then the core.

topic_questions.text: A lunar eclipse occurs when the
options: Moon is farthest from the Sun
Earth lies between the Sun and the Moon
Sun lies between the Earth and the Moon
Moon lies between the Sun and the Earth
topic_questions.explanation: The Earth's shadow falls on the Moon during a lunar eclipse.

topic_questions.text: A solar eclipse occurs when the
options: Earth is nearest to the Sun
Earth lies between the Sun and the Moon
Moon lies between the Sun and the Earth
Sun lies between the Earth and the Moon
topic_questions.explanation: The Moon blocks sunlight from reaching part of the Earth.

topic_questions.text: The International Date Line roughly follows longitude
topic_questions.explanation: The International Date Line is based on the 180° meridian, opposite the Prime Meridian.

topic_questions.text: A traveller crossing the International Date Line from west to east
options: repeats a day (goes back one day)
topic_questions.explanation: Crossing eastward, the calendar date is set back by one day.

topic_questions.text: The distance between two successive degrees of latitude is approximately
topic_questions.explanation: A degree of latitude is about 111 km, since the Earth's circumference is about 40,000 km.

topic_questions.text: The circumference of the Earth is approximately
topic_questions.explanation: The Earth measures roughly 40,000 km round the Equator.

topic_questions.text: The shortest distance between two points on the Earth's surface lies along a
topic_questions.explanation: A great circle divides the globe into equal halves and gives the shortest route between two places.

topic_questions.text: Lines of latitude are also called
topic_questions.explanation: Lines of latitude run east-west and are parallel to the Equator.

topic_questions.text: All lines of longitude meet at the
topic_questions.explanation: The meridians converge at the poles and are farthest apart at the Equator.

topic_questions.text: Latitude is defined as the angular distance of a place
options: from the centre of the Moon
north or south of the Equator
east or west of the Equator
topic_questions.explanation: Latitude is measured in degrees north or south of the Equator.

topic_questions.text: Longitude is defined as the angular distance of a place
options: north or south of the Equator
north or south of the Prime Meridian
east or west of the Prime Meridian
topic_questions.explanation: Longitude is measured in degrees east or west of the 0° meridian.

topic_questions.text: The Earth is nearest to the Sun at a position called
topic_questions.explanation: Perihelion occurs in early January, when the Earth is closest to the Sun.

topic_questions.text: The Earth is farthest from the Sun at a position called
topic_questions.explanation: Aphelion occurs in early July, when the Earth is farthest from the Sun.

topic_questions.text: The Sun is classified as a
topic_questions.explanation: The Sun is a star and the centre of our solar system.

topic_questions.text: The Moon is the Earth's natural
topic_questions.explanation: The Moon orbits the Earth and is its only natural satellite.

topic_questions.text: The deflection of winds to the right in the Northern Hemisphere is caused by the
topic_questions.explanation: The Earth's rotation deflects moving air to the right in the north and to the left in the south.

topic_questions.text: Nigeria uses a standard time that is
topic_questions.explanation: Nigeria is in West Africa Time, which is GMT+1.

topic_questions.text: Areas within the polar circles experience the 'midnight sun' in
topic_questions.explanation: In summer, the polar regions have continuous daylight for part of the period.

topic_questions.text: The outermost layer of the Earth is called the
topic_questions.explanation: The crust is the thin, solid outer shell of the Earth.

topic_questions.text: The continental crust is composed mainly of
topic_questions.explanation: Sial is the lighter, granitic material that makes up the continents.

topic_questions.text: The oceanic crust is composed mainly of
topic_questions.explanation: Sima is the denser, basaltic material that underlies the ocean floors.

topic_questions.text: The central part of the Earth is believed to consist mainly of
topic_questions.explanation: The core, called nife, is rich in nickel and iron.

topic_questions.text: Rocks formed from the cooling and solidification of magma are called
topic_questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten material cools and hardens.

topic_questions.text: Granite is an example of a(n)
topic_questions.explanation: Granite cools slowly beneath the surface, so it is an intrusive igneous rock.

topic_questions.text: Basalt is an example of a(n)
